evidence: At 230 8C Ni(thd)2 saturates the surface at a pulse length of 1.5 s corresponding to a dose of 3 /C210/C06 mol per pulse. Saturation with water was reached after 4.5 s which corresponds to a dose of 3 /C210/C04 mol per pulse, an excess of roughly 100 times the Ni(thd)2 dose. The optimized pulse sequence consists of 4.5 s H2O/8 s purge/1.5 s Ni(thd)2/8 s purge at 230 8C. At 275 8C a 6 s water pulse is needed to reach saturation and uniform film thickness over larger areas i.e., an even larger water excess compared to 230 8C (insert b, Fig. 1). The initial nucleation process is studied by atomic force microscopy (AFM) and reveals nucleation of well-separated grains which coalesce to a continuous film after about 250 ALD cycles.
